lines.line: Summary: A ghost found on every board that robs another player of coins or a Star. The Boo Bell item calls one up whenever you want, and a Boo can also serve as a Duel Mode partner.

quoted: Boos are features on every board
They are part of the returning Boo Bell item once more.
One is partnered with Yoshi by default in Duel Mode Partners
Boo will steal coins or a star from another player if you use the Boo Bell to ring him up.

lines.line: Weak points: If you hold a Boo Repellant, a Boo that tries to rob you of coins or a Star sets it off automatically and runs away empty-handed. As a duel partner, a Boo that gets attacked hits back with the same amount of damage before vanishing, but it does not strike back at a Thwomp, and strikes back at a Chain Chomp only when it stands directly in front.

quoted: When Boo tries to steal coins or a Star from a player holding a Boo Repellant, the item automatically activates, spraying gas at Boo and causing him to flee without stealing anything.
If attacked, will counter-attack for equal damage before disappearing.
it counterattacks an opponent (except Thwomps) to deliver equal damage, and does this to Chain Chomp only if it is directly in front.

lines.line: Tips: On Waluigi's Island a Boo gives you a choice of two paths instead, though one is rigged and returns you to the start. When you ring a Boo up with the Boo Bell, he asks who the target is and what to take. In Duel Mode, Yoshi begins with a Boo as his partner.

quoted: Boos have a unique role in Waluigi's Island, where they present two paths to the player character upon being encountered: one of them is rigged and leads to the start, while the other allows the player character to continue along.
One is partnered with Yoshi by default in Duel Mode Partners
The player who uses this item summons Boo. Boo then asks who the player wants Boo to steal from and what to steal.

lines.line: Summary: When you land on a Bowser Space, Bowser shows up. Most often he goes after your coins, but he may also give out items or put a curse on all the players.

quoted: Bowser Space
If this space is landed on, then Bowser appears. He usually tries to steal Coins from players. He may also give players certain items, or cast curses on all players.

lines.line: Weak points: In Mario Party 3 the roulette is not left to chance. It stops on whatever event the pointer is over at the moment you press the button, so careful timing lets you choose. A player with no coins is spared: Bowser pays you instead, 30 coins, or 40 or 50 depending on where you rank, no event takes place and no Stars are lost.

quoted: Unlike in previous games, the result of the Bowser Event roulette is not random, allowing the player to select an event from those available with precise timing; the roulette always stops on the event that the cursor is hanging over when

If a player without any coins lands on a Bowser Space, Bowser pays them either 30, 40, or 50 coins (depending on placement) and does not trigger an event. Unlike in the first Mario Party, no Stars are lost if the player possesses any when this happens.

lines.line: Looks like: Bowser flashes a color when an event starts: purple for Bowser's Curse, green for Bowser's Reverse Curse, yellow for Bowser Shuffle and red for Bowser Revolution.

quoted: Bowser Revolution: This event is unchanged from the previous games mechanically, but Bowser now flashes red during this event.
Bowser's Curse: Bowser flashes purple
Bowser's Reverse Curse: Bowser flashes green
Bowser Shuffle: Bowser flashes yellow

lines.line: Tips: Bowser's Curse forces all four players, on their following turn, to move just 1 to 3 spaces, as a Poison Mushroom would. Bowser's Reverse Curse sends them backwards instead, as a Reverse Mushroom would. Either curse can be cancelled by an item that counters it. Bowser Shuffle mixes up where the four players stand, and he can also give you a free Bowser Phone (very rarely two) or a free Bowser Suit.

quoted: Bowser's Curse: Bowser flashes purple, then places a curse on all four players that forces them to move 1–3 spaces on their next turn, much like a Poison Mushroom, unless they use an item that cancels the effect.

Bowser's Reverse Curse: Bowser flashes green, then places a curse on all four players that forces them to move backwards on their next turn, much like a Reverse Mushroom, unless they use an item that cancels the effect.
Bowser Shuffle: Bowser flashes yellow, then uses his magic to randomly shuffle all four players' positions on the board.
Bowser Phone Giveaway: Bowser gives the player a Bowser Phone for free. Rarely, Bowser gives the player two Bowser Phones.
Bowser Suit Giveaway: Bowser gives the player a Bowser Suit for free.

sections.name: Game Guy and the Game Guy Space

lines.line: Summary: A game-show host who takes all your coins when you land on his space, then runs a luck-based minigame in which you either get them back doubled (or more) or lose them all. Game Guy Spaces turn up in both Party Mode and Duel Mode.

quoted: If the player lands on that space, Game Guy flies by, takes all of their coins, and then leads the player to a Game Guy minigame. These mostly luck-based minigames determine if the player takes the coins back doubled (or more, depending on the minigame) or if they lose them all.
Game Guy Space
Players who land on this space have to hand over all of their Coins to Game Guy.
Game Guy Space
When a player lands on this space, then they must hand over all of their Coins to Game Guy.

lines.line: Weak points: His four minigames are Game Guy's Lucky 7, Magic Boxes, Roulette and Sweet Surprise, and they depend mostly on luck. A typical result is that you double your coins or lose the lot, although you can gamble for bigger multiples.

quoted: Game Guy's Lucky 7
Game Guy's Magic Boxes
Game Guy's Roulette
Game Guy's Sweet Surprise
These mostly luck-based minigames
Game Guy owns four minigames: Game Guy's Lucky 7, Game Guy's Magic Boxes, Game Guy's Roulette, and Game Guy's Sweet Surprise.
Players can usually double their coins or lose all coins, though they can risk their money for higher multiples.

lines.line: Looks like: A Shy Guy with a yellowish mask and a bowtie.

quoted: He is a Shy Guy who sports a yellowish mask, a bowtie, and a natural showman's attitude.

lines.line: Tips: The Lucky Charm item sends a chosen player, even yourself, to a Game Guy minigame without landing on his space. In Game Guy's Room you can practise: you start with 10 coins, may bet up to 100, and aim to reach 1,000, and winning earns you Mario's Puzzle Party Pro, a rare minigame. The room itself only opens once Story Mode has been finished with eight or more S rankings.

quoted: Players can also call Game Guy on themselves or other players by using the Lucky Charm without needing to land on his space.

Here, the player is given 10 coins and can bet any number of coins held, up to 100 coins. The goal is to reach 1,000 coins, but losing all of them ends the game. Winning this challenge unlocks the Rare minigame Mario's Puzzle Party Pro
The Story Mode must be beaten with at least eight S rankings for this room to be unlocked.

lines.line: Summary: Woody's unfriendly twin on the Woody Woods board. Stop on a Happening Space by Evil Woody and you must take one of two costly fruits: a Reverse Block Fruit (you roll, but move backwards) or a Minus Coin Fruit (you lose five coins).

quoted: Evil Woody is Woody's counterpart who debuts in Mario Party 3 in Woody Woods.
he will award them a Minus Coin Fruit (resulting in a loss of five coins) or a Reverse Block Fruit allowing the player to roll again but go in reverse.

Action Time also happens when a player lands on a Happening Space at the Evil Woody. He makes the player choose from one of these two fruits: a Minus Coin Fruit (which takes away five Coins from the player) or a Reverse Block Fruit (which makes the player roll a Dice Block and go in reverse).

lines.line: Weak points: You choose one of the two fruits yourself, but if you pick neither Evil Woody always gives you the Reverse Block Fruit, so the only way to avoid the backwards move is to choose the Minus Coin Fruit.

quoted: If the player does not choose either fruit, Evil Woody will always give them a Reverse Block Fruit.
If the player fails to select a fruit in either of these events, they will forcibly receive the dice-related option.

lines.line: Looks like: A tree whose color palette is the inverse of Woody's, blue with purple leaves, with a perpetually angry expression.

quoted: Contrasting with Woody's perpetually happy expression and kind-hearted attitude, Evil Woody has a perpetually angry expression and a hostile attitude. His color palette is also an inversion of Woody's color palette, being blue with purple leaves.

lines.line: Tips: Three ? Spaces ring Evil Woody. The friendly Woody on the same board offers good fruits instead: a Plus Block Fruit that gives a second dice roll, or a Plus Coin Fruit worth five coins. If you choose neither, he gives you the extra Dice Block.

quoted: if a player lands on one of the three ? Spaces surrounding Evil Woody
a Plus Coin Fruit (which gives the player five Coins) or a Plus Block Fruit (which makes the player roll the Dice Block a second time)
The player can decide not to choose either fruit; by doing so, Woody always gives an extra Dice Block to the player.

sections.name: Deep Bloober Sea's torpedo and anglerfish traps

lines.line: Summary: Creatures in Deep Bloober Sea can shift you across the board: a Sushi in a submarine can fire you onto the other path, a giant vacuum anglerfish can pull you in and spit you out again, and a giant Blooper Baby calls for its mother, whose tentacle carries you over to the far side.

quoted: Every time players get here, the shark makes them press one of four buttons before taking the path they chose.
Landing on a Happening Space near the giant Blooper Baby makes it call for its mother, whose huge tentacle takes the player to the other side of the board.
Action Time happens when someone lands on a Happening Space next to a giant vacuum anglerfish.

lines.line: Weak points: At the submarine junction you press one of four buttons: three are harmless and one sends a torpedo that knocks you onto the opposite path. The button layout stays fixed until someone presses the wrong one, and now and then the Sushi simply does not see you and lets you through. Against the anglerfish, keep tapping the button to struggle against the pull, or it swallows you.

quoted: Three buttons do nothing, allowing safe passage, but one fires a torpedo at the player, blasting them to the opposite path. Additionally, the buttons do not reset until the incorrect one is chosen. Sometimes the Sushi will fail to notice the player, allowing them to safely pass by.
Players need to tap to swim against the suction. Anyone who fails is sucked into the fish

lines.line: Looks like: A Sushi (a shark) in a submarine looking over the main junction, a giant vacuum anglerfish with an arrow on it that spins, and a giant Blooper Baby.

quoted: the main one is looked over by a Sushi in a submarine.
giant vacuum anglerfish
The arrow on the fish spins around
the giant Blooper Baby

lines.line: Tips: The anglerfish's spinning arrow settles pointing down, to the front or to the right. A player it swallows ends up close to a Sushi, close to Boo, or at the starting point. The board has 93 spaces in all, 5 of them Bowser Spaces and 2 Game Guy Spaces.

quoted: The arrow on the fish spins around, then points to the bottom, the front, or the right.
landing near a Sushi, Boo, or back at the start.
Bowser Spaces
Game Guy Spaces
Total of Spaces

sections.name: Waluigi's Island's dynamite and rigged path

lines.line: Summary: An unlockable board full of traps. Every landing on a Happening Space on the dynamite island lowers a counter that begins at 5; at 0 the dynamite goes off, and every player caught in the blast forfeits all their coins.

quoted: Waluigi's Island is the unlockable

every time someone lands on one, the number in the center of the explosives counts down. It always starts on 5, but when it gets to 0, the dynamite explodes. Anyone caught in the blast loses all their coins
When this number reaches zero, it causes an explosion that covers the entire circle. Any players that are caught in the explosion lose all of their Coins.

lines.line: Weak points: To leave the dynamite island you hit the gear at the middle of the board in the Action Time. Whichever arrow is lit as you land shows the path you have to follow; if it stops on the down arrow, or you act too slowly, you are stuck on the island. On the road to Boo there are two paths, and one is booby-trapped and returns you to the start.

quoted: players who want to get off the dynamite island activate the gear in the center of the board.
The arrow that is flashing when they land is the path they have to take (if it stops at the down arrow, or if players take too long to act, they stay in the dynamite island).
Players that want to get to Boo have to take one of two paths, where one of them is booby trapped. If they take the path that has the trap, they are sent back to the start.

lines.line: Looks like: An island of dynamite with a counter in the middle of the explosives that begins at five, and a gear at the board's center with four arrows that light up one after another, clockwise.

quoted: the number in the center of the explosives counts down. It always starts on 5
The four arrows on it (up, right, down, and left) flash in clockwise order at a random speed.

lines.line: Tips: On the dynamite island the Happening Spaces are the ones to fear. On the island in the upper left every space turns into a different type each turn, apart from the Bank Space, and on the upper sides of the board the red pipes always carry you to the green pipe by the start.

quoted: The Happening Spaces are dangerous here
Every turn, the spaces change to another type of space.
The one space that never changes is the Bank Space
Wherever players go on the topsides of the board, they will always go to into red pipes that lead them to the green pipe near the start

lines.line: Summary: A chainless Chain Chomp that can be a Duel Mode partner; its attack hits the opponent and all their partners at once. Its attack is 1, its stamina 2 and its salary six coins.

quoted: Chain Chomp
None
Attacks opponent and all partners simultaneously.
Chainless Chain Chomps can be partners in Duel Mode after unlocking them from the lottery and have a health value of 2; an attack of 1; and a salary of six coins.

lines.line: Weak points: A Boo partner counterattacks against a Chain Chomp's multi-hit only when it stands right in front of that Chain Chomp.

quoted: Will not attack back if hit by a Thwomp or a Chain Chomp in its multi-attack if it is not directly in front of the attacking Chain Chomp.

lines.line: Looks like: Chain Chomps are black or dark blue balls with large round eyes and a wide open mouth full of razor-sharp teeth; the Duel Mode partner comes without a chain.

quoted: Chain Chomps resemble a black or dark blue ball, sometimes with chains attached to them.
They have big circular eyes, large gaping mouths, and razor-sharp teeth.
Chainless Chain Chomps can be partners in Duel Mode

lines.line: Tips: No character begins with a Chain Chomp; you win one from the partner lottery. A powered-up Chain Chomp swells to Shark Chomp size, leaps and slams down on every opponent. Pairing a Bob-omb with a Chomp makes the Millennium Star comment on the pair, but the attack is not raised.

quoted: Chain Chomp
None
Attacks opponent and all partners simultaneously.
Powered Up: It grows to the size of a Shark Chomp, jumps up, and then body slams all opponents.
The following combinations causes the Millennium Star to comment on it, but the attack does not get raised.
Bob-omb and Chomp make a dangerous duo!

lines.line: Summary: A Duel Mode partner whose attack is 0, yet it flattens any of the enemy's partners in one go and leaves the enemy player untouched. It has 2 stamina and a salary of four coins.

quoted: Although it has zero attack, it can attack partners and defeats them instantly; but does nothing to the opposing player.
Thwomp has 0 attack and 2 HP, but he can also defeat any partner instantly, though he does nothing against players.
Thwomp's salary is four coins per turn.

lines.line: Weak points: Used against you, it takes out your partners in one hit and does nothing to you, the player. A Boo partner that a Thwomp defeats does not hit back as it normally would.

quoted: He can take out your opponent's partner in one blow but won't touch your opponent.
he can also defeat any partner instantly, though he does nothing against players. If a Boo is defeated by a Thwomp, it will not retaliate like it normally would.

lines.line: Looks like: A blue, cube-shaped block of stone with the up-to-date Thwomp face on it; the colour and the shape are the original ones.

quoted: Thwomps use a more cubic version of their Super Mario 64 design in the first six console games and Mario Party Advance.
These Thwomps now have their modern facial design, but retain their original blue, cubic shape.

lines.line: Tips: No character begins with a Thwomp, so one can only turn up through the partner roulette. With two Thwomps, the Millennium Star reduces their salaries by one rather than raising their attack, and it also remarks on a Whomp and Thwomp pairing. The instruction booklet states an attack of 2 by mistake.

quoted: A Thwomp is also a partner in Duel Mode, exclusively through the roulette, because no character has a Thwomp as their initial partner.
If the player has two Thwomps partners, the Millennium Star decreases their salaries by one, and their attack is not boosted by one.
Whomp and Thwomp make an earth shaking combination!
The instruction booklet incorrectly states that Thwomp has an attack stat of 2 instead of 0.

lines.line: Summary: A spray can that makes Boo flee without stealing from you. Toad sells it for 10 coins, and the manual spells it Boo Repellent.

quoted: Boo Repellant (spelled Boo Repellent in the manual) is an item found in Mario Party 3.
Boo Repellant
10 Coins

lines.line: Uses: While you hold it, it sets itself off the moment Boo moves to take your coins or a Star, and Boo runs off with nothing. A can can be used only once.

quoted: When Boo tries to steal coins or a Star from a player holding a Boo Repellant, the item automatically activates, spraying gas at Boo and causing him to flee without stealing anything.
Each can is good for one use.

lines.line: Tips: At the start of your turn you may discard one to free up space, and that counts as your item use for the turn. Other players are put off trying a Boo steal on you, so its effect often lasts a long time, but computer players ignore it and go ahead regardless, Stars included.

quoted: It is possible for a player to throw away a Boo Repellant at the start of their turn to make room in their inventory, which counts as using an item for that turn.

since other players will be deterred from wasting a Boo attempt against it, its overall effect can last for much longer. CPU players do not care and will try regardless, even attempting to steal Stars from players who have one.

lines.line: Summary: Rings up Boo to steal coins or a Star from an opponent. Baby Bowser sells it for 15 coins.

quoted: Boo Bell
The player who uses this item summons Boo. Boo then asks who the player wants Boo to steal from and what to steal.
15 Coins
where he sells items such as Lucky Lamps, Reverse Mushrooms and Boo Bells.

lines.line: Uses: Using it calls up Boo, who asks you to name the victim and the loot. From the target he takes either coins or a Star.

quoted: The player who uses this item summons Boo. Boo then asks who the player wants Boo to steal from and what to steal.
Boo will steal coins or a star from another player if you use the Boo Bell to ring him up.

lines.line: Tips: Anyone carrying a Boo Repellant sends Boo away and loses nothing. Baby Bowser's shop, which mainly sells items for hindering opponents, is where the Boo Bell is sold.

quoted: When Boo tries to steal coins or a Star from a player holding a Boo Repellant, the item automatically activates, spraying gas at Boo and causing him to flee without stealing anything.
Baby Bowser mainly sells items that can be used to hinder opponents.
where he sells items such as Lucky Lamps, Reverse Mushrooms and Boo Bells.

lines.line: Summary: A treasure chest that takes an item from an opponent of your choosing. Only Baby Bowser's shop sells it, for 10 coins, and Princess Peach likes it best of all items.

quoted: A Plunder Chest is a recurring item in the Mario Party series. It is a treasure chest that can steal an item from another player.
Mario Party 3
10 Coins
Only available in Baby Bowser's Shop.
In Mario Party 2 and Mario Party 3, it is Princess Peach's favorite item
Plunder Chest
10 Coins

lines.line: Uses: You choose the opponent to rob; if they hold several items, which one is taken is left to chance. You cannot use the loot until after you have rolled.

quoted: When the player uses this item, the player gets to choose an opponent to steal an item from. If the designated player has more than one item, the item stolen is chosen randomly.
the Plunder Chest steals a random item from an opponent of the user's choosing, and the received item cannot be used before rolling.

lines.line: Tips: The Barter Box is similar, but the Plunder Chest takes just one item, whereas the Barter Box trades over all of them. When Peach is computer-controlled she goes for it ahead of other items if she can.

quoted: The Plunder Chest works in a similar way; however, the Plunder Chest only steals one item.
When used, the Barter Box exchanges all of the player's items with the items of another player.
meaning that as a CPU player she will prioritize it over other items if possible.

lines.line: Summary: A lamp that holds Mushroom Jeanie, who moves the Star to a different space. Baby Bowser's shop sells it for 10 coins, and it is the counterpart of the Magic Lamp.

quoted: Lucky Lamp
When used, the Mushroom Jeanie appears. She then moves the Star somewhere else, essentially making it the counter-part of the Magic Lamp.
10 Coins
The Lucky Lamp is an item found only in Mario Party 3. It is essentially a counterpart to the Magic Lamp.

lines.line: Uses: Mushroom Jeanie appears at the Star Space when it is used and relocates the Star elsewhere on the board, rather than carrying you to it as the Magic Lamp does.

quoted: Upon being called, the Mushroom Jeanie will appear at the Star space to move it to another location
Instead of taking the player to the Star Space, it moves the Star to a different space on the board.
On your command, Mushroom Jeanie will move the Millennium Star to a new location.

lines.line: Tips: On Spiny Desert, which has a mirage Millennium Star, she always heads for the real one. Baby Bowser's shop sells the Lucky Lamp, and an item minigame can award it too.

quoted: in Spiny Desert, where there is a Millennium Star mirage on the board, she will always go to the real Millennium Star.
The Lucky Lamp can be bought from Baby Bowser for a little less than a Magic Lamp, and it can also be won in an item minigame.

lines.line: Summary: Rings Bowser up so that he runs one of his events on a player of your choice, just as if that player had stepped on a Bowser Space. It is sold at Baby Bowser's shop for 10 coins.

quoted: When used, the player calls Bowser. Bowser then asks who is calling him, the player chooses one of the players (can be the caller). Bowser then performs his events to that player as if the player landed on a Bowser Space.
10 Coins
Bowser Phones are sold in Baby Bowser's Item Shops

lines.line: Uses: You pick an opponent, or yourself, to be on the receiving end of one of Bowser's events, and you may look over the board first. There is also an option that leaves the choice to Bowser, who then picks a random player.

quoted: The player then chooses one of their opponents (or themselves) to have Bowser make them do one of his events, as if they landed on a Bowser Space. The player can also view the board before making a selection. Selecting "Who do you think?" results in Bowser choosing a random player.

lines.line: Tips: The player you choose really does go to see Bowser, at the castle spot the Bowser Space uses. You can also be given a Bowser Phone free of charge by a Bowser Space.

quoted: the player actually goes to meet Bowser at the same castle location as the Bowser Space.
may be given for free from a Bowser Space.

lines.line: Summary: A rare coin bearing Game Guy's picture on one side. Using it makes a chosen player stake all their coins on a Game Guy minigame. Neither shop sells it.

quoted: The Lucky Charm is an item in Mario Party 3. It is a coin depicting Game Guy on one side. Using the Lucky Charm forces the target, which can be the user, to risk all of their Coins in a Game Guy minigame.
Wacky Watches, Barter Boxes, Koopa Kards, and Lucky Charms are never sold by either Toad's Trading Post or Baby Bowser's Joint

lines.line: Uses: Using it calls Game Guy, who collects every one of the target's coins and starts a Game Guy minigame. The target may be another player or yourself.

quoted: When a player uses this item, they summon Game Guy. Game Guy then takes all of the player's Coins, and a Game Guy minigame is initiated. This can also be used to force another player to play a Game Guy minigame.
The Lucky Charm lets you send another player to the Game Guy Room to risk all of his or her coins.

lines.line: Tips: Toad can hand you one when you land on an Item Space, a hidden block rarely holds one, and so can an Item Bag bought at Baby Bowser's Joint.

quoted: A Lucky Charm can be obtained from an Item Space by meeting Toad or rarely from a hidden block.
If purchased from Baby Bowser's Joint, the Item Bag may contain a rare item: a Lucky Charm.

lines.line: Summary: A rare item that moves the game straight to five turns from the finish. No Item Shop sells it.

quoted: A Wacky Watch is a rare item appearing only in Mario Party 3. It cannot be bought in any Item Shop
it sets the game's turn number to exactly five turns before the game ends.

lines.line: Uses: Using it sets the game to the point where five turns are left, so it can cut a game very short, or stretch it out if used when fewer than five turns remain.

quoted: it sets the game's turn number to exactly five turns before the game ends. This can drastically shorten the game, or make it longer when it is used in turns closer than five to the game's end.
When used, this rare item sets the game to such a time that there are five turns left.

lines.line: Tips: Toad can give you one on an Item Space, and a Hidden Block can hold one too. It is unique among this game's items in never being sold in a shop or found in an Item Bag. If you use it on what would have been the last turn, the remainder of that turn still counts as the last, so the Item Shops stay shut.

quoted: players can get it by meeting Toad on an Item Space or finding it in a Hidden Block.
If a Wacky Watch is used on what would otherwise be the final turn, the game is still played as if it were the final turn for the remainder of the turn (i.e., Item Shops are still closed).
The Wacky Watch is the only item in Mario Party 3 that cannot be purchased from an Item Shop or Item Bag.
It is not possible for an Item Bag from either shopkeeper to contain a Wacky Watch.
